CHARGER

A rocket that drops a sensor payload at apogee and streams five channels of telemetry to a handheld ground station. We built CHARGER and it won.

How it worksAirframe + payload / 2026

How it works

01

The event

A G motor flies the rocket to 700-1,200 feet. On the way down the payload releases the nose cone at 75 percent of peak altitude, and the nose cone has to land under 15 feet per second on its own.

With the nose cone gone, a camera on the payload films the ground until it lands.

02

The airframe

37 inches, single stage, 2.68 inches across, four trapezoidal balsa fins on a cardboard body tube. Center of gravity at 22 inches, stability margin 1.80 calibers.

Cardboard because the payload transmits from the pad on, and carbon fiber would put a conductive shell around the 2.4 GHz antenna.

Explore all 28 components in 3D.

03

The numbers

Aerotech G77R-7, thrust to weight 8.17. Simulated apogee 1,033 feet. Descent 13.8 feet per second under a 48 inch ripstop nylon canopy.

04

What the rules forced

The event bans commercial flight computers in the payload, so every ejection charge fires off our own board and barometric sensor. The commercial altimeter is only there so a judge can read peak altitude after recovery.

05 / Launch day

We got two clean flights away on the first day, then put up the qualifying flight before noon on the second.

06

The result

Final standings, published by Union College, April 23, 2026.

  1. Union College Rocket Club
  2. Chantilly Aerospace Club Team 3
  3. Thomas Jefferson High School
  4. Spring Grove Area High School Team 2
  5. George Mason University

Details
  • Length 37 in, maximum diameter 2.68 in, single stage
  • Four trapezoidal fins, root chord 2.76 in, height 2.36 in, sweep 2.17 in
  • Stability margin 1.80 cal, centre of gravity at 22 in
  • Aerotech G77R-7, thrust to weight 8.17, burn 1.25 s
  • Simulated apogee 1,033 ft, descent 13.8 ft/s on a 48 in parachute
  • Rail buttons at 2 in from the aft end and 22 in from the nose, near the CG
  • Rocket $465.42, payload $250.53, ground station $0.00 from existing kit
